question: On 24 July 2025, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways hosted which event in New Delhi to deliberate on financial strategies for India’s maritime future?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maritime Financing Summit, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maritime Financing Summit, 2025** was organized by the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** (MoPSW) on **24 July 2025** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The summit served as a critical platform to deliberate on **financial strategies** and **investment frameworks** necessary to propel India toward its goal of becoming a global maritime power.
 
• The primary objective of the event was to foster a dialogue between **policymakers**, **financial institutions**, and **industry stakeholders** to unlock the investment potential within the maritime sector.
 
• The discussions were strategically aligned with the **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047**, which envisions an investment of over **Rs. 80 trillion** to transform the maritime infrastructure of the country.
 
• The event highlighted the importance of **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)** and innovative funding mechanisms like **Maritime Development Funds** to support port modernization and shipping fleet expansion.
 
• Key focus areas included **sustainable financing** for green shipping initiatives and the enhancement of **Ease of Doing Business** in the maritime financial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047:**
 
 
• Launched to outline the roadmap for the next **25 years**, this vision aims to increase the capacity of Indian ports to **10,000 MTPA** (Million Tonnes Per Annum) by **2047**.
 
• It focuses on **port-led industrialization**, **coastal shipping**, and the development of **Smart Ports** through **digitization** and **Automation**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW):**
 
 
• This ministry is the apex body responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to **ports**, **shipping**, and **inland water transport** in India.
 
• Under the leadership of **Shri Sarbananda Sonowal** (as of recent administrative records), the ministry has prioritized the **Sagarmala Project** to reduce logistics costs.
 
 
 
• **Investment Opportunities in Maritime Sector:**
 
 
• India offers **100% FDI** (Foreign Direct Investment) under the automatic route for **port construction and maintenance projects**.
 
• The **Blue Economy** policy of India aims to contribute significantly to the **national GDP** by utilizing ocean resources sustainably while ensuring environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Green Shipping and Sustainability:**
 
 
• The **Harit Sagar Guidelines 2023** emphasize the reduction of **carbon footprints** at ports and the promotion of **renewable energy** integration.
 
• India is working toward establishing **Green Hydrogen Hubs** at major ports like **Deendayal Port** and **Chidambaranar Port**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Logistics Efficiency:** One of the core themes of the **2025 Summit** was to lower India's **logistics cost** from **13-14%** of GDP to the global average of **8%**.
 
• **Global Rankings:** India aims to enter the top **10** in the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI)** by improving port turnaround times and **multimodal connectivity**.
 
• **Major Ports:** Currently, India has **12 Major Ports** and over **200 non-major ports**, which together handle approximately **95%** of the country's foreign trade by volume.
 
• **Shipbuilding Industry:** The government is promoting the **Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP)** to encourage domestic vessel manufacturing and reduce dependency on foreign ships.
